Commandant.
Shanghai Municipal Council.
C. I. D.
I. O. REG
No.
Date
January 24th
1916
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)
Sir,
It is reported that General Yang received a code telegram on 22nd inst instructing him to dispatch as many field guns and rifles and as much ammunition as he can spare to Peking, as quickly as possible.
A code telegram has also been received by Admiral Liu instructing him to finish the construction as soon as possible of two river boats which are being made in Kiangnan dock.
It is reported that General Yang of Shanghai and General Tsu of Chekiang favour the anti-monarchists. It is said that they will declare independence as soon as Nanking goes over.
It is reported that none of the City Police are loyal, and that they intend to loot as soon as trouble starts.
It is reported that the rebels here intend to send circulars to all the Magistrates of this province warning them against sending money collected in taxes to Peking at the present time as they usually do on the approach of the Chinese new year.
It is reported that General Feng □□ of Nanking has instructed Mr.Zee Koh Liang □□□ Chief of the Shanghai-Woosung Police to order all the newspapers published in the district under his control to date their papers according to the new monarchical calendar. The order must be obeyed within three days and the offices of newspapers failing to obey will be sealed up.
It is reported that Mr. Yang Tcheng has received instructions from the Central Government to remain all the time in Shanghai and to take care that the rebels do not gain the sympathy of foreigners.
In consequence of a report that the rebels had bought four aeroplanes from the Japanese, General Yang has been instructed to be ready to cope with an aerial attack on the Arsenal or any other strategic point.
It is now reported in rebel circles that the rebels here will rise on 4th Prox.
A memorial service in honour of the two Constables, who lost their lives during the recent outbreak in Shanghai, was held in the Central Fire Station in the City yesterday. Several of the City officials and a large number of the City Police under their Chief Mr. Zee Kou Liang, were present.
over
（批：Endorsed on / wed Jan. 25 / Seen by / Lwd Springfield）
pages.zh:
司令官。
上海工部局。
刑事侦缉处。
I. O. REG
编号
日期
1916年
1月24日
警务处，
（侦探科）
先生：
据报，杨将军于本月22日收到一封密电，指示他尽快将尽可能多的野战炮、步枪及弹药调往北京。
刘海军上将也收到一封密电，指示他尽快完成在江南船坞建造的两艘江轮的施工。
据报，上海的杨将军和浙江的朱将军倾向反君主制派。据说一旦南京倒戈，他们即宣布独立。
据报，华界警察均不忠诚，并打算一旦发生动乱即行抢劫。
据报，此地的反叛者意图向本省所有知县发出通函，警告他们不要像往年中国新年临近时那样，将征收的税款汇往北京。
据报，南京的冯□□将军已指令上海-吴淞警察局局长子谷良（音译）先生，命令其管辖区域内出版的所有报纸按照新的君主制历法标注日期。该命令必须在三天内执行，违者报馆将被查封。
据报，杨正（音译）先生已接到中央政府指令，须常驻上海，并确保反叛者无法获得外国人的同情。
鉴于有关反叛者从日本人手中购买了四架飞机的报告，杨将军已受命做好准备，以应对针对兵工厂或其他任何战略要地的空中袭击。
现据反叛者圈内消息，此地的反叛者将于下月4日起事。
昨日，在城内中央救火会举行了一场追悼会，以纪念在最近上海骚乱中丧生的两名巡捕。多名华界官员以及在其局长子谷良（音译）先生率领下的大量华界警察出席了仪式。
续后
（批注：签署于 / 1月25日星期三 / Lwd Springfield 阅）

Shanghai Municipal Council.
24
191
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL · JUNCTA JUVANT · POLICE FORCE）
POLICE FORCE,
(DETECTIVE BRANCH)
2
At 4.15 p.m. 23rd inst a fire broke out in a dwelling
house in Pay Yuen alleyway near the Kiangnan Arsenal.
The blaze quickly spread to the adjoining houses thirty
of which were gutted. The outbreak was caused through
a bed curtain accidently catching fire.
Some members of the local German community staged a
play in the Olympic theatre on Saturday night. The performance
was attended by the German residents and their friends.
It is reported that the profits will be used to assist
German prisoners who escaped from Siberia.
Your Obedient Servant,
Chief Detective Inspector.
Captain Superintendent of Police.

上海工部局。
24
191
（印章：上海工部局 · 同心协力 · 警务处）
警务处，
（侦探科）
2
本月23日下午4时15分，江南兵工厂附近百源里（音译）的一处住宅发生火灾。
火势迅速蔓延至邻近房屋，其中三十间被烧毁殆尽。起火原因系床帷意外着火所致。
部分当地德国侨民于周六晚在奥林匹克大戏院上演了一出戏剧。德国居民及其朋友观看了演出。
据报，所得利润将用于援助从西伯利亚逃脱的德国战俘。
您顺从的仆人，
总探长。
警务处总监。
